assertion.text:
Erdős Problem #847: declared status 'disproved'. Formalized: yes. Let $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set for which there exists some $\epsilon>0$ such that in any subset of $A$ of size $n$ there is a subset of size at least $\epsilon n$ which contains no three-term arithmetic progression.

Is it true that $A$ is the union of a finite number of sets which contain no three-term arithmetic progression? Prize: no. Tags: additive combinatorics.
